messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Estonian, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Estonian line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Kui ma langesin tagasi madalasse kohta, enne mu silmi ilmus kes pärast pikka vaikust näis kähisev.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Source → Estonian)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|------------------|--------| | Mentre | temporal conjunction “while” | Kui | “when / while” | OK | | ch'i' | “che io” – first‑person pronoun “I” (subject) | ma | “I” | OK | | rovinava | imperfect verb “was falling / going down” | langesin | “I fell / was falling” | OK | | in | preposition of direction “to / into” | tagasi | “back” (covers direction) | OK | | basso | adjective “low” | madalasse | “to low (place)” | OK | | loco | noun “place, location” | kohta | “place” | OK | | dinanzi | adverb/preposition “before (in front of)” | enne | “before” | OK | | a | preposition “to” (introduces *li occhi*) | – | – | **UNNECESSARY** (Estonian does not need a separate preposition here) | | li | definite article “the” (plural) | – | – | **UNNECESSARY** (articles are omitted in Estonian) | | occhi | noun “eyes” | silmi | “eyes” (partitive) | OK | | mi | dative pronoun “to me” (experiencer) | mu | “my” (possessive) | OK | | si | reflexive/impersonal pronoun in passive construction | – | – | **UNNECESSARY** (passive formed without it) | | fu | auxiliary verb “was” (past remote) | – | – | **UNNECESSARY** (auxiliary omitted) | | offerto | past participle “offered / presented” | ilmus | “appeared / showed up” | OK | | chi | relative pronoun “who / one who” | kes | “who / that” | OK | | per | preposition “through” (means/causation) | pärast | “after” | **WRONG** (semantic shift: “through” → “after”) | | lungo | adjective “long” | pikka | “long (acc.)” | OK | | silenzio | noun “silence” | vaikust | “silence” (genitive) | OK | | parea | verb “seemed” | näis | “seemed / appeared” | OK | | fioco | adjective “hoarse / weak” | kähisev | “hoarse / raspy” | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `a`, `li`, `si`, `fu` – these function words are not required in Estonian and are naturally omitted. - **WRONG**: `per` – rendered as **pärast** (“after”) instead of a more faithful “through” sense; this changes the temporal/causal nuance.
All other source tokens are correctly represented in the Estonian translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Estonian script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Estonian text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 61** - Original: Kui ma langesin tagasi madalasse kohta, - Issue: none - Corrected: Kui ma langesin tagasi madalasse kohta,
- **Line 62** - Original: enne mu silmi ilmus - Issue: none - Corrected: enne mu silmi ilmus
- **Line 63** - Original: kes pärast pikka vaikust näis kähisev. - Issue: WRONG – “pärast” (“after”) does not convey the intended “through”. - Corrected: kes läbi pika vaikuse näis kähisev.
